subject: PharmaLine: in-region processing guarantees + erasure flow
messages:
From: Sophie Müller <sophie.mueller@pharmaline.de>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver Gruber <oliver.gruber@legalconsult.de>, procurement@pharmaline.de
Date: Mon, 18 Sep 2028 09:12:00 +0200
Subject: Question on EU-only processing and downstream exports

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at PharmaLine is excited about Redwood's inference performance. Before we proceed to procurement, legal has a couple of technical questions to confirm EU-only processing for our workload and what evidence you can provide under Schrems II/SCCs. High level asks:

- Can you confirm that inference payloads from EU tenants will not be routed outside the EU at any point (control plane vs data plane distinction)?
- If we sign SCCs plus the in-region addendum, what operator access controls exist (console/SSH/remote debug) and how are those access events logged?
- Backups and snapshots: are there backups that live outside the EU or cross-border replication for restore? If so, what's the deletion/retention guarantee?

Would appreciate a short write-up we can share with legal — if you have a sample execution of SCCs or an attestation we can include that would help accelerate the review.

Best,
Sophie Müller
Head of IT Compliance
PharmaLine GmbH
[Attachment: product-brief.pdf]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Müller <sophie.mueller@pharmaline.de>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Sep 2028 11:34:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Question on EU-only processing and downstream exports

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise summary you can pass to legal; attaching a short ops diagram and a preview of the SCCs execution page for context. Happy to hop on a quick call if Oliver wants to walk the document.

Summary answers (brief):

1) Data plane locality: when you choose an EU-only deployment we provision compute and storage in EU regions only. All inference requests, KV caches, and long-term logs for that tenant remain in the selected EU region(s). The control plane (management API) is in our control plane region but does not retain customer prompt/response data. For critical edge cases (failover events) we will only fail over to another EU region unless customer explicitly allows cross-border failover.

2) SCCs + in-region addendum: we have an SCCs addendum that binds the operator access controls and logging obligations. Key points:
- Operator access is role-based and requires just-in-time elevation with MFA and approval.
- Live debugging access requires a recorded session and is limited to named operators; ephemeral SSH is disabled for in-region-only tenants unless legally required and pre-approved.
- Audit logs are retained for 13 months by default; we can provide more granular export of operator session records on request.

3) Backups and snapshots: primary backups are stored in the same EU region. We do not replicate backups to non-EU regions for in-region-only customers. Backups are retained per the retention schedule you select; we offer a certified deletion job that wipes backups and provides a deletion manifest. Typical timeline for full deletion from production + backups is 30 days after a confirmed erasure request (accelerated options available).

Next steps: I attached two files: "redwood-inregion-ops-diagram.png" (ops boundaries and routing) and "SCCs-execution-preview.pdf" (preview of the SCCs signature workflow and addendum language we propose). If Oliver wants, we can run the standard template through legal and produce a redline-friendly bundle.

If that works, I'll loop Lauren to check billing/SLA implications for the in-region guarantee.

Cheers,
Irene Choi
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-inregion-ops-diagram.png]
[Attachment: SCCs-execution-preview.pdf]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Sep 2028 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: PharmaLine: in-region processing guarantees + erasure flow

Irene — looping Marcus for legal language and SLA notes. A few internal points for your record:

- Procurement will likely want an explicit SLA clause that forbids non-EU failover except for declared emergency. That's a negotiable add-on; we should surface potential credits if we accept a strict ban on cross-border failover.
- For operator access: legal will request the list of named operator IDs and the JIT approval flow steps. Marcus — can you prepare a one-page operator access attestation and sample audit export?
- Retention/deletion: confirm the 30-day deletion manifest process and whether backups on object-store are overwritten vs. tombstoned. Sophie asked for a cryptographic wipe vs logical delete; we should state the default and optional approach.

Action items: Marcus to draft attestation (by EOD tomorrow), Irene to confirm failover behavior wording and run pricing impact with sales.

-LB

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Müller <sophie.mueller@pharmaline.de>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Sep 2028 16:45:00 +0200
Subject: Re: PharmaLine: in-region processing guarantees + erasure flow

Hi all — attaching the operator-attestation draft and a short note on backup deletion semantics. Quick answers inline:

- Named operators: we provide a CSV with operator IDs and job roles (example attached). Access requests require a 2-step approval (team manager + security approver) and are logged to an immutable audit stream.
- Deletion semantics: primary delete performs object tombstoning followed by scheduled garbage collection which overwrites blocks within 30 days. For customers requiring cryptographic key destruction we can offer KMS key destruction on retained encrypted snapshots to prevent decryption after the deletion window (this is an add-on and will affect retention guarantees).
- SLA language suggestion: "Redwood will not initiate cross-border data failover of production inference traffic for in-region-only customers except as required by law or with prior written consent from the customer." We can discuss credits tied to the strictness level.

I've uploaded the attestation and the backup note to the shared doc (link below) and started a DocuSign template for the SCCs addendum so legal can route it internally.

Links:
- Attestation + backup note: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1abcdExamplePharmaPlan
- DocuSign template: https://app.docusign.com/templates/EXAMPLE-12345

Sophie — happy to schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to run through the attestation if you like.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: operator-attestation-draft.docx]
